entities.summary: Mark John Douglas Messier is a Canadian former professional ice hockey forward. His playing career in the National Hockey League (NHL) lasted 25 seasons (1979–2004) with the Edmonton Oilers, New York Rangers, and Vancouver Canucks. He also played professionally with the World Hockey Association (WHA)'s Indianapolis Racers and Cincinnati Stingers. He also played a short four-game stint in the original Central Hockey League (CHL) with the Houston Apollos in 1979. He was the last WHA player to be active in professional ice hockey, and the last active player in any of the major North American professional sports leagues to have played in the 1970s.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key player in the Edmonton Oilers' dynasty of the 1980s, Messier won five Stanley Cup championships and was named the Conn Smythe Trophy winner twice. His on-ice accomplishments cemented his status as one of the greatest players in NHL history.
